business_problem: Nsano needed a database platform that could scale its payments business, eliminate downtime and failed requests from its legacy managed deployment, reduce operating costs, and support faster rollout of new financial services.
solution_summary: Nsano moved from a problematic third-party managed MongoDB Community deployment to MongoDB Atlas so it could scale digital payments services without hand-managing reliability and security work. The platform handles mobile money aggregation, remittances, and bulk transaction processing across more than 30 African countries and the UK, so the team needed a data model that could keep changing with new services. Atlas preserved that flexibility while adding security defaults, operational guidance, and the headroom to break a monolithic application into microservices. After the May-to-July 2024 migration, database failures and processing bottlenecks disappeared, query optimization suggestions became part of normal operations, and Atlas features such as encryption and caching reduced compliance risk and infrastructure sprawl. With Atlas as the standard backend, Nsano can launch new services quickly and keep engineering focused on application delivery instead of database firefighting.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Provides Nsano's managed payments data platform, replacing its unreliable legacy deployment and supporting microservices growth.

data_flow: Payment and transaction data from Nsano's mobile money, remittance, and bulk-processing services is persisted in MongoDB Atlas, where application services query and update it, automated recommendations help optimize performance, and the same shared backend supports new microservices as they are launched.
business_outcome: Nsano reduced database costs by about 25%, cut service launch times from six weeks to two weeks, improved compliance posture, and expanded from a few monolithic services to fourteen microservices running on Atlas.
